newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tietmeyer - DAX surge not sign of lack of liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer - DAX surge not sign of lack of liquidity.

text.p: Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said on Thursday he did not wish to comment on the recent surge in the German DAX share index but added that the rise did not reflect a lack of liquidity in the economy.
"We of course follow it (the DAX) very closely, but I won't make any comment like the head of the U.S. central bank," Tietmeyer told a news conference.
He was referring to famous comments from Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan who recently said U.S. financial markets were suffering from "irrational exuberance".
"The central bank must watch all factors, but the DAX is not a money factor like M3 (money supply)," Tietmeyer said.
Tietmeyers said that many of the DAX member companies in Germany were heavily engaged in the export sector.
Germany's export sector has been boosted in recent months by a sharp depreciation in the mark versus the dollar, making German goods cheaper aborad.
"One shouldn't overlook the fact that the DAX doesn't represent the whole economy," Tietmeyer said.
